rv.q: The charming new Broadway incarnation of The Fantasticks, lovingly directed and choreographed by Christopher Gattelli, ... plants itself firmly in the present, and comes to unexpected bloom.
It's a Fantasticks for the longtime fans, and a warm invitation to the uninitiated to forgive its slight corniness and succumb to its gentle charms.

Gattelli's joyous staging maintains the charm, wit, and warmth of this unimpeachable show, even if the move to a bigger stage at times reminds audiences why it succeeded on more intimate ones.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this queer reimagining of the beloved classic, praising its charm and joyful staging. A few find the gender-swap superficial, but most agree the show's timeless warmth translates well to its long-overdue Broadway debut.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's smallest houses (597 seats) and one of its newest, built in 2015 as Second Stage's permanent home. The intimate scale means excellent sightlines from nearly every seat, though the modern design prioritizes function over grandeur.

acc.note: Elevator from lower lobby to Mezzanine. LOOP system for t-coils and cochlear implants.
